_comment: Trust policy for magik-deploy-role (the role cd.yml assumes via GitHub OIDC).
ALL THREE sub patterns are required, and the reason is the single most common
GitHub-OIDC failure mode:
* cd.yml's `promote-production` job declares `environment: production`.
The MOMENT a job references a GitHub Environment, the OIDC subject claim
changes format to `repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<name>` — it NO
LONGER carries the ref. A trust policy matching only `ref:refs/tags/*`
therefore rejects it with 'Not authorized to perform
sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity', which is exactly what happened on CD
* cd.yml's `deploy-staging` job declares `environment: staging` for the
same reason (staging gate, added alongside this comment) — same failure
mode, same fix: its own explicit `environment:staging` sub pattern.
* the `ref:refs/tags/*` pattern is kept so any future job in this workflow
that does NOT use an environment still works.
All three remain tightly scoped to this one repository — a fork, another
repo, or a branch push cannot assume this role.
NOTE: this file documents the intended trust policy; applying it to the
real IAM role in AWS (e.g. `aws iam update-assume-role-policy`) is a
separate, manual step — see docs/runbooks/ci-cd.md 'Staging gate'
prerequisites.
